lines: The night barge takes no fare. The bargeman just says the House already paid.
Bargeman: Vellmarch? Night barge. No fare. The House already paid for you.

bell_crypt_candle_thief: Jost: I take the grave candles back to Tallowmarket. They sell them again. Very thrifty, the dead.
bell_crypt_candle_thief_defeat: Jost: Caught. Take a candle. It's only slightly used.
bell_crypt_candle_thief_intro: Jost: You didn't see me. I'll make sure of it.
bell_crypt_marsh_guide: Runhild: I guide people through the marsh. Half fare in advance. I've never had to collect the second half.
bell_crypt_marsh_guide_defeat: Runhild: The way out is up the stairs. That advice is free. My first.
bell_crypt_marsh_guide_intro: Runhild: Lost? Good. Lost people pay best.
bell_crypt_rope_warden: Hilde: Forty ropes hang down here. I know every one by its pull. Three of them pull back.
bell_crypt_rope_warden_defeat: Hilde: Rung like a bell. I'll be humming for a week.
bell_crypt_rope_warden_intro: Hilde: Don't touch the ropes. Touch me instead, see what happens.
bell_crypt_sign: The marsh took the chapel and kept the cellar. The bell ropes still hang down through the roof.
bellrope_marsh_bellwalker: Edda: Every bell rope in this marsh leads to someone who rang for help. None of them were answered.
bellrope_marsh_bellwalker_defeat: Edda: The marsh will have me one day. Not today, it seems.
bellrope_marsh_bellwalker_intro: Edda: Ring if you need help. I'll pretend I didn't hear.
bellrope_marsh_peat_poacher: Ragna: I dig peat where the House says not to. The things I find there, the House says not to mention.
bellrope_marsh_peat_poacher_defeat: Ragna: Fine, it's a shame for me. Mind the soft ground. It's occupied.
bellrope_marsh_peat_poacher_intro: Ragna: You saw my spade. That's a shame for one of us.
cindergate_quay_bunkhouse_docker: Docker Bram: Six bunks, nine dockers. Nobody asks where the other three sleep.
cindergate_quay_customs_store_keeper: Storeman Tibb: Seized goods. Some were seized twice. Once by us, once from us.
cindergate_quay_folk_1: Docker Haldis: I load crates for the House by day. At night I unload them for the Syndicate. Same crates.
cindergate_quay_folk_2: Tollman Rusk: Looking at the toll booth is a copper. Asking about it is two.
cindergate_quay_folk_3: Net Widow Oona: My husband fell in the harbour. The House sent flowers. The Syndicate sent the bill for the flowers.

lines: Dock Nurse Ottilie: Sit. Your Spirlings look seasick. I charge the House, not you. For now.

cindergate_quay_net_loft_mender: Net Mender Saffi: I mend the nets the Syndicate cuts. They pay me to mend them, too.
cindergate_quay_sign: Cindergate Quay. Tolls payable on arrival, departure and complaint.
cindergate_quay_tollhouse_clerk: Toll Clerk Mabry: Entry is a copper. Leaving is two. Staying is a matter for the House.

lines: Chandler Brisk: Rope, tonics, alibis. Two of those are on the shelf.
cindergate_quay_trader.action: shop strong_tonic max_tonic remedy cooling_gel wake_bell revival_leaf dash_brew guard_brew pith_mend pith_clear

foundry_rift_acolyte: Gert: Brannoc says the Syndicate rusted the furnace. The Syndicate says Brannoc did. The furnace says nothing.
foundry_rift_acolyte_defeat: Gert: Hot work. Brannoc's hotter. Good luck.
foundry_rift_acolyte_intro: Gert: You want the foundry? Sweat for it.
foundry_rift_sign: The cold furnaces of the foundry. Rust grows here like moss, and faster.

lines: Cold water seeps between the stones. It tastes of iron and old debts.
Your Spirlings drink and rest.

hookwick_boatshed_boatwright: Shipwright Kaja: This hull has two names painted on it. Both owners swear it's theirs.
hookwick_eel_smokery_smoker: Smoker Hennig: The eels don't mind the smoke. They stopped minding anything a while ago.
hookwick_folk_1: Lockkeeper's Boy Wim: Odile pays me to say she's out. She's always out. Even when she's in.
hookwick_folk_2: Eel Seller Grete: The canal water rose to my door. The eels came in to look at the rent.
hookwick_folk_3: Boatwright Jory: I build every boat twice. Once for the man who pays, once for the man who steals it.

lines: Harbour Aunt Bel: Sit down before you fall in. Everyone falls in eventually. Some get pushed.

hookwick_lock_office_clerk: Lock Clerk Pim: Odile is out. She is always out. Leave a bribe after the tone.
hookwick_sign: Hookwick. Every boat has two owners. Ask either; both are lying.
hookwick_tackle_shop_angler: Old Angler Fritha: I caught a boot today. It still had a foot in it. Not a good foot.
larkspur_heights_counting_house_banker: Banker Quillon: Your money is perfectly safe with us. Your name is another matter.
larkspur_heights_folk_1: Opera Usher Lenz: Tonight's opera ends with a duel. Last week's ended with a funeral. Same tenor.
larkspur_heights_folk_2: Maid Ilka: I polish the masks for the ball. Some of them are still warm.
larkspur_heights_folk_3: Retired Duelist Corvo: I lost one eye in an honest duel. The other in a dishonest one. Guess which taught me more.

lines: House Physician Aurel: Rest here. Discretion is included in the price. The price is also discreet.

larkspur_heights_mask_atelier_maskmaker: Maskmaker Orla: Each mask fits one face. I keep a list of whose.
larkspur_heights_salon_noble: Lady Vespera: Duels are so vulgar. I have mine fought for me.
larkspur_heights_servants_hall_maid: Footman Erich: We hear everything upstairs. We are paid to forget it. We are paid badly.
larkspur_heights_sign: Larkspur Heights. Clean streets. High walls. Short memories.

lines: Glove Merchant Ysette: Our tonics are imported. So is our conscience. Neither has arrived.
larkspur_heights_trader.action: shop strong_tonic max_tonic remedy cooling_gel wake_bell revival_leaf dash_brew guard_brew pith_mend pith_clear

lastlamp_bell_house_ringer: Rope Boy Ned: I count the bell rings in a ledger. The ledger is getting heavy.
lastlamp_folk_1: Bell Ringer Ash: I ring the marsh bell when someone goes missing. My arms are very strong.
lastlamp_folk_2: Pawnbroker Wex: Corin's men pawn their medals here. I sell them back to Corin. Everyone wins but the medals.
lastlamp_folk_3: Gravekeeper Ivo: The marsh keeps the bodies. I just keep the names. Fewer complaints.

lines: Lamplighter Nan: Sit under the lamp. Out there, nobody comes back to sit anywhere.

lastlamp_lamp_store_lamplighter: Wick Keeper Sten: We have oil for one more year. After that, the marsh gets the street.
lastlamp_name_room_keeper: Scribe Ulla: Names of the lost, one per line. I leave a blank line at the end. Just in case.
lastlamp_pawnshop_pawnbroker: Pawn Clerk Lisbet: Medals, rings, a wooden leg. All pawned, none collected.
lastlamp_sign: Lastlamp. The last lit street before the marsh. Keep to the light.
lock_rift_acolyte: Senn: Odile sold the lock to the Syndicate. Then sold the Syndicate a second lock. She's very good.
lock_rift_acolyte_defeat: Senn: Go on. Mind the key. It's already been copied.
lock_rift_sign: Rusted lock gates hold back water that isn't there. Odile keeps the only key.

lines: Cold water seeps between the stones. It tastes of iron and old debts.
Your Spirlings drink and rest.

masque_rift_acolyte: Liesl: Sable gave me a mask on my first day. I haven't seen my own face since. I don't miss it.
masque_rift_acolyte_defeat: Liesl: Bravo. Sable will want to meet you. She'll want to be you, too.
masque_rift_acolyte_intro: Liesl: Masks off. Oh, you don't have one. Then this will hurt more.
masque_rift_sign: Under the opera house the masks are stacked to the ceiling. None of them have eyes.

lines: Cold water seeps between the stones. It tastes of iron and old debts.
Your Spirlings drink and rest.
Tenor Alban: They boo me. Every night, third act, the same six voices. Somebody is paying for it. Nobody boos that well for free.
Tenor Alban: Find out who. I am an artist. I have no enemies. Only colleagues.
Tenor Alban: Fitz carries my scarf again. I check it for pins.
Lady Amalia: The boos? Bought at the Counting House, dear. Account 'A Friend of Music'. So is the applause. Different account.
Lady Amalia: The claque itself drinks out on Smelter's Drift. Ask them who the friend is. Bring something to hit them with.

q2_bought_boos_amalia_after: Lady Amalia: I never boo. I simply leave, loudly.

lines: Claque Leader Bruno: Who pays for the boos? That's trade knowledge. You want it, you audition.

q2_bought_boos_claque_after: Claque Leader Bruno: The understudy pays for boos. The tenor pays for bravos. We do both in one evening. It's honest work, if you hum.

lines: Claque Leader Bruno: Bravo. Fine. It's Fitz, the understudy. He pays Tuesdays. And in spring the tenor paid us to boo Fitz. We're very fair.

q2_bought_boos_doubt: Tenor Alban: That was criticism. Paid criticism is still criticism.
q2_bought_boos_fitz: Fitz: I carry the scarf. I've had it lengthened. No reason.
q2_bought_boos_fitz_defeat: Fitz: Off key. Me. On the one night someone was listening.
Fitz: Tell him the fourth act is his. I'll have the fifth. There's a death in the fifth.
q2_bought_boos_fitz_intro: Fitz: Alban sent you. He sends everyone. He once sent me for his scarf during my own solo.

lines: Tenor Alban: Fitz is on Smelter's Drift. Don't touch his throat. I want him to hear himself lose.
Tenor Alban: Fitz. My understudy. Little Fitz, who carries my scarf. He pays six men to boo me so he can sing the fourth act.
Tenor Alban: He waits on the drift tonight to pay them again. Go. Silence him. Artistically.
Tenor Alban: I have never paid a claque in my life. You believe that, of course.
Tenor Alban: You beat him? Bravo! Here, from my dressing room. The claque works for me again. They always did, on weekdays.
q2_bought_boos_reward.action: set_flag q2_bought_boos_paid; give_item guard_brew 2; quest_stage q2_bought_boos 4

lines: Tenor Alban: You beat him. And you know about spring. Here. Twice the brew. An artist pays for silence. It's the only review that counts.
q2_bought_boos_reward_doubt.action: set_flag q2_bought_boos_paid; give_item guard_brew 4; quest_stage q2_bought_boos 4

q2_bought_boos_trust: Tenor Alban: 'Maestro.' Say it again. Slower.
q2_bought_boos_wait: Tenor Alban: The ladies in the Quiet Salon know who pays for what. And the claque drinks on Smelter's Drift, where nobody hears them practise.

lines: Lamp Boy Nils: The lamps on the marsh edge go out, one a night. Somebody steals the oil. Then people stray off the path.
Lamp Boy Nils: Find the oil thief. I'm only a boy. I just find the purses in the morning. To hand in.
Reed Woman Alma: The oil thief? A small one, with a can. Pours the oil in the marsh, puts the lamp out, sits down and waits.
Reed Woman Alma: In the morning he walks the edge with a sack. Whistling. A child's tune.

q2_dark_lamps_alma_after: Reed Woman Alma: I keep to the dark. Nobody robs you in the dark here. They wait for you to leave it.

lines: Oil Boy Gerd: Every can is counted. One goes out each night for 'the night round'. Signed with an N.
Oil Boy Gerd: There is no night round. Ask the reed folk on the Bellrope Marsh where the can goes.

q2_dark_lamps_gerd_after: Oil Boy Gerd: Oil for one more year, Sten says. Less, the way it's going.

lines: You take Nils's sack: four tonics, eleven left boots and a lamp key. The lamps on the edge burn again that night.
q2_dark_lamps_nils_sack.action: set_flag q2_dark_lamps_paid; give_item max_tonic 4; quest_stage q2_dark_lamps 4

q2_dark_lamps_nils_sack_after: Nils: I light the lamps now. All of them. Nan watches me do it. Every one.
q2_dark_lamps_nils_sack_defeat: Nils: Not fair. You're bigger. Everybody's bigger.
Nils: Take the sack. It's only tonics. The purses I already handed in. To me.
q2_dark_lamps_nils_sack_intro: Nils: Help! Thief! Oil thief! That's my line, anyway. Nobody's awake to hear it.

lines: Lamp Boy Nils: A small one with a can, pouring it into the marsh? Small. Well. I haven't grown much this year.
Lamp Boy Nils: No lamp, no path. No path, they stray. They stray, they drop things. I find the things. I'm good at finding.
Lamp Boy Nils: I asked you so there'd be a thief to blame. You'll do. Strangers always do.

q2_dark_lamps_wait: Lamp Boy Nils: The oil is counted in the Lamp Store. And the reed folk on the Bellrope Marsh see who walks the edge at night.

lines: Rent Man Odd: My tenants vanish the night before rent day. Six this year. I worry about them. I worry about the rent more, but still.
Rent Man Odd: Find out where they go. I only want to help them. With the arrears.
Runaway Frauke: Odd sold me the passage himself. 'A fresh start, no rent.' The boat turned for the foundry before the first bridge.
Runaway Frauke: Don't tell him where I am. He'll say he's worried. He always says he's worried.

q2_eel_rent_frauke_after: Runaway Frauke: I sleep in the hedge. The hedge has never raised the rent.

lines: Smoke Boy Lüder: The tenants? They leave by boat, the night before rent day. Somebody pays their passage. They look so grateful.
Smoke Boy Lüder: One jumped off at the bend and ran up the Rookery Cut. She wasn't grateful any more.

q2_eel_rent_lueder_after: Smoke Boy Lüder: The eels all go the same way too. Nobody asks them either.

lines: You take Odd's cooling gel and his passenger list. Six names are crossed out. The seventh is Frauke. The eighth is yours.
q2_eel_rent_odd_boat.action: set_flag q2_eel_rent_paid; give_item cooling_gel 4; quest_stage q2_eel_rent 4

q2_eel_rent_odd_boat_after: Odd: I've lowered the rent. Nobody believes me. That's the worst of it.
q2_eel_rent_odd_boat_defeat: Odd: Evicted. Me. From my own quay.
Odd: Take the gel. It's for the foundry burns. The tenants won't be needing it. They've stopped coming back.
q2_eel_rent_odd_boat_intro: Odd: The night boat has one seat free. I'd hate to waste it.

lines: Rent Man Odd: She told you I sell the passage myself. Well. A landlord provides. Shelter, then transport.
Rent Man Odd: The boat goes to the foundry. Brannoc pays per head. The tenants work off the rent. Some pay in years. Rent is rent.
Rent Man Odd: I sent you to find the one who got away. You found her. Thank you. You've a strong back yourself, I notice.

q2_eel_rent_wait: Rent Man Odd: The Eel Smokery looks out on the night boats. And runaways go inland by the Rookery Cut.

lines: Widow Hette: My Ludo died at the foundry. His last wages never came. The paymaster says they were paid. To whom?
Widow Hette: Find Ludo's wages. It's not the money. It is the money. But it's also the principle of the money.
Widow Hette: Ludo stays dead on paper. It's the best he's ever looked.
Slag Carter Bero: The pay cart? Goes down the Slag Tunnels every week, full. Comes up empty. No workers down there. Not live ones.
Slag Carter Bero: There are stairs off the drift. The bruisers at the bottom don't like questions. Or answers.

q2_ghost_wages_bero_after: Slag Carter Bero: I cart slag. Slag never asked for a raise.

lines: Tunnel Bruiser Ortwin: The payroll is private. So is this tunnel. So is your face, in a minute.

q2_ghost_wages_bruisers_after: Tunnel Bruiser Ortwin: Forty names, all dead, all paid. Signed with a hook on the L. I don't read. I was told about the hook.

lines: Tunnel Bruiser Ortwin: Enough. Take the payroll. Forty dead men on it, and one very lively signature.
Widow Hette: He counts in the Slag Tunnels. Go and make me a widow properly. In the financial sense.

q2_ghost_wages_ludo: Ludo: Forty-one wages. She always was better with money than I was.
q2_ghost_wages_ludo_defeat: Ludo: Short. The till is short. That has never happened to a dead man before.
Ludo: Tell her I died well. Tell her I died twice, if it helps.
q2_ghost_wages_ludo_intro: Ludo: Hette sent you. She always did send other people. Stand there, you're in my light.

lines: Widow Hette: Forty dead men on the payroll, still drawing wages. And the paymaster signs with a little hook on the L. Like Ludo did.
Widow Hette: He isn't dead. He's the paymaster. He pays himself my widow's wage and I wore black for it.
Widow Hette: You beat him? Good. He pays me forty-one wages now. His own and the forty. Here. A widow can be generous.
q2_ghost_wages_reward.action: set_flag q2_ghost_wages_paid; give_item max_tonic 3; quest_stage q2_ghost_wages 4

q2_ghost_wages_wait: Widow Hette: The slag carters on Smelter's Drift haul more than slag. And the pay cart goes down into the Slag Tunnels.

lines: Baker Joss: Somebody bought a rumour about my bread. 'Joss bakes with foundry ash.' A heavy one. My shop is empty.
Baker Joss: Find the buyer. I've never done anything to anyone. Not that anyone could weigh.
Baker Joss: Jutta and I share a stall now. We split the customers and the rumours. Mine are heavier.

q2_heavy_rumour_doubt: Baker Joss: Two pounds. 'Jutta's raisins have legs.' It was a light rumour. A joke, really.

lines: Rumour Girl Ebba: The ash bread? Four pounds, paid in flour. We don't get paid in flour often. It gets in the gossip.
Rumour Girl Ebba: The buyer's mark is in the Weigh House book. Everything heavy is.

q2_heavy_rumour_ebba_after: Rumour Girl Ebba: A good rumour keeps a week. A true one goes off by supper.

lines: Baker Joss: Jutta is on the Tollchain Causeway with her cart. Tell her the truth hurts. Then show her.
Scale Girl Gundel: Four pounds, ash bread. Signed with a pretzel. That's the bakery by the quay. Jutta's.
Scale Girl Gundel: Line above it: two pounds, 'raisins with legs', signed with a loaf. I'm sure that's nothing.

q2_heavy_rumour_gundel_after: Scale Girl Gundel: I only weigh. If I started judging, there'd be a queue.
q2_heavy_rumour_jutta: Jutta: We share a stall. I count the till. He counts me counting.
q2_heavy_rumour_jutta_defeat: Jutta: Ask him who bought the first rumour. Ask him what he signs with.
q2_heavy_rumour_jutta_intro: Jutta: Joss sent you? Did he tell you about my raisins? No. He wouldn't.

lines: Baker Joss: My sister. Jutta. With the bakery by the quay. My own sister bought four pounds of lies about me.
Baker Joss: She comes up the causeway with her cart every evening to take my customers home. Stop her.
Baker Joss: I never started this. You do believe I never started this?

choices.text: How heavy was your first one?

lines: Baker Joss: You beat her? Bless you. Here, from the shop. Jutta says I bought the first rumour. A rumour, that. I sold it on already.
q2_heavy_rumour_reward.action: set_flag q2_heavy_rumour_paid; give_item remedy 2; quest_stage q2_heavy_rumour 4

lines: Baker Joss: You beat her, and you know about the raisins. Here. Double. Remedies. For whatever you might be tempted to say.
q2_heavy_rumour_reward_doubt.action: set_flag q2_heavy_rumour_paid; give_item remedy 4; quest_stage q2_heavy_rumour 4

q2_heavy_rumour_trust: Baker Joss: Thank you. It's a relief to hear it from someone I'm not paying.
q2_heavy_rumour_wait: Baker Joss: Rumours are sold in the Rumour Room and weighed in the Weigh House. Somebody signed for mine.

lines: Mother Gesa: A bell rings out in the marsh every night. My Tobin went missing a week ago. The ringer says nobody rings it.
Mother Gesa: Find the bell. The Lamp Guild has been very kind. They've already offered to buy his room.
Mother Gesa: Tobin rents out his own room now. To the Guild. At a criminal price. I'm so proud.

q2_marsh_bell_collector: Asmus: I've been moved to accounts. There are no ropes in accounts. Only ledgers. They hang you slower.
q2_marsh_bell_collector_defeat: Asmus: Lights out. That's our line, usually.
Asmus: Take the boy. The Guild will find another saving. The street is full of mouths.
q2_marsh_bell_collector_intro: Asmus: The mother sent you with her answer? I'd hoped for a signature. A fight is so much paperwork.
q2_marsh_bell_doubt: Mother Gesa: You've met mothers before, I see.

lines: Mother Gesa: The collector waits in the Bell Crypt, by the ropes. Bring my boy up. And the collector's purse.
Reed Cutter Keld: The night bell? One rope goes down, not up. Into the old chapel cellar. There are stairs in the reeds.
Reed Cutter Keld: I cut round it. A bell that rings from below is asking for someone else.

q2_marsh_bell_keld_after: Reed Cutter Keld: The reeds grow back. That's more than you can say for most things here.

lines: Mother Gesa: Alive. In the crypt. Put there by the Guild, so the street has one lamp less to pay for.
Mother Gesa: And they sell the rooms of the lost. Mine was next, I suppose. Two for one.
Mother Gesa: The Guild's collector comes tonight for my answer. I could sign. Tobin eats a great deal. What would you do?

choices.text: You'd never sign. I'll stop him.
I'll stop him before you can sign.

lines: Mother Gesa: Tobin is home. He's eaten everything. Here are his bells, he's not to touch a rope again. I did keep the Guild's offer. To frame.
q2_marsh_bell_reward.action: set_flag q2_marsh_bell_paid; give_item wake_bell 2; quest_stage q2_marsh_bell 4

lines: Mother Gesa: Tobin is home. You looked at me the whole way as if I'd sign. Here, all the bells in the house. Now stop looking.
q2_marsh_bell_reward_doubt.action: set_flag q2_marsh_bell_paid; give_item wake_bell 4; quest_stage q2_marsh_bell 4

lines: Tobin: You heard me! A week I've been ringing. The Lamp Guild walked me down here. 'Fewer mouths, fewer lamps,' they said.
Tobin: Tell my mother. And tell her not to sign anything. She likes signing things.

q2_marsh_bell_tobin_after: Tobin: I'll keep ringing till the collector is gone. It annoys him. It's all I've got.
q2_marsh_bell_trust: Mother Gesa: Never. Well. Hardly ever. Thank you for thinking so.
q2_marsh_bell_wait: Mother Gesa: The reed cutters on the Bellrope Marsh follow the ropes. Follow them.

lines: Old Varn: My medal. For the stand at the Tithe Bridge. Some thief pawned it while I slept. A hero's medal, in a pawnshop.
Old Varn: Find out who pawned it. I'd go myself, but my leg. And my other leg.
Pawn Boy Kord: The bridge medal? Pawned on the first of every month. Same shaky hand. The ticket says 'Varn'.
Pawn Boy Kord: The name on the medal isn't Varn, though. It says 'Reik'. The Counting House in Larkspur pays a Reik every month.

q2_pawned_medal_kord_after: Pawn Boy Kord: Everything in here is somebody's proudest day. Marked down.

lines: Old Varn: The ticket is in my name, and the pension is in Captain Reik's. Yes. Both are in my pocket.
Old Varn: Reik held the bridge. I held Reik's coat. When he fell, I was right behind him. Very close behind.
Old Varn: I pawn the medal each month and send someone to ask who did it. They bring it back for free. You were meant to stop at the pawnshop.
Clerk Sidonie: Captain Reik's pension? Collected every month, in person. Remarkable, for a man who fell off the Tithe Bridge.
Clerk Sidonie: An old man with two bad legs signs for it. He runs down our stairs afterwards.

q2_pawned_medal_sidonie_after: Clerk Sidonie: We never ask if a client is alive. It would halve the business.

lines: You take Varn's tonics and the medal. On the back somebody scratched: 'Watch the one holding your coat.'
q2_pawned_medal_varn_reik.action: set_flag q2_pawned_medal_paid; give_item strong_tonic 4; quest_stage q2_pawned_medal 4

q2_pawned_medal_varn_reik_after: Varn: My legs are much worse now. Honestly, this time.
q2_pawned_medal_varn_reik_defeat: Varn: Beaten. From the front. Nobody has ever done that to me. I never let them.
Varn: Take the tonics. They're on Reik. Everything is on Reik.
q2_pawned_medal_varn_reik_intro: Varn: I pushed a captain off a bridge, child. Guess what I do to errand runners.
q2_pawned_medal_wait: Old Varn: The Pawnshop keeps every ticket. And the Counting House in Larkspur pays the bridge pensions.

lines: Maid Petra: At the ball somebody wore my mistress's mask. Her face, her walk, her signature. My mistress was in bed with a headache.
Maid Petra: Find the second face. Madam cries so, and I'm the one who has to iron the handkerchiefs.
Coachman Henner: The lady? I drove her from the ball to the Counting House at midnight. She tipped. That's how I knew it wasn't her.
Coachman Henner: Signed for the whole account with her left hand. And she smelled of starch.

q2_second_face_henner_after: Coachman Henner: I drive, I don't look. Looking costs extra and I've never been offered it.

lines: You take the brews from Petra's travelling bag. Under them lie three more masks. One of them is yours.
q2_second_face_petra_lady.action: set_flag q2_second_face_paid; give_item guard_brew 3; quest_stage q2_second_face 4

q2_second_face_petra_lady_after: Petra: Madam irons her own handkerchiefs now. She's dreadful at it.
q2_second_face_petra_lady_defeat: Petra: Unmasked. In the street. How terribly middle class.
Petra: Take the brews. They were for the journey. The money stays where it is. In me.
q2_second_face_petra_lady_intro: Petra: You may address me as Madam. Briefly.

lines: Maid Petra: The lady signed with her left hand? How odd. Madam is right-handed. I'm left-handed. What a coincidence.
Maid Petra: Fifteen years I've carried her face to the cleaner. I know it better than she does. It fits me better, too.
Maid Petra: The account is empty and the headache was in the tea. You were meant to find a stranger. Pity. Now I need a third face.
Mask Boy Tilo: Lady Vespera's mask? We made it twice. The second one was ordered through the servants' door, paid in small coin.
Mask Boy Tilo: Fifteen years of small coin, I'd say. Ask the coachmen on the Tithe Road where the second face went.

q2_second_face_tilo_after: Mask Boy Tilo: A good mask shows who you are. A very good one shows who you'd rather rob.
q2_second_face_wait: Maid Petra: Masks are made in the Mask Atelier. And the coachmen on the Tithe Road know who rode where that night.

lines: Mina: My father was lock clerk before Pim. He sits in the cells for copying Odile's key. He can't even copy a signature.
Mina: Find out who really cut the copies. Please. He's all I have. He and the house, and the house is in his name.
Mina: I visit Father on Sundays. He's proud of me. He doesn't know why yet.
Bait Boy Enno: Fritha hooked a lump of wax last week. A key pressed in it. Big key. Lock-gate big.
Bait Boy Enno: It floated out of the Smugglers' Culvert, under the Weeping Locks. There's a cutter down there called Hask.

q2_seven_keys_enno_after: Bait Boy Enno: Worms don't lie. That's why nobody here keeps them long.

lines: Mina: The runner is in the Smugglers' Culvert. Bring me the slip. Only the slip. Don't read it.
Key Cutter Hask: Odile's key? Seven copies. Best work I ever did. A Syndicate runner brought the wax and the coin.
Key Cutter Hask: The old clerk? Never saw him. A girl collected the keys. Polite. Counted them twice.

q2_seven_keys_hask_after: Key Cutter Hask: I kept an eighth. A man needs a pension.

lines: Mina: Seven copies, ordered by a Syndicate runner. So it wasn't Father. Thank you. Oh, thank you.
Mina: The runner still has the order slip. With the slip Father walks free. Get it from him. He hides in the culvert.
Mina: The slip! Signed by me, yes. I told you not to read it. Father stays where he is. The house needed a clear name on it. Here. For not telling.
q2_seven_keys_reward.action: set_flag q2_seven_keys_paid; give_item revival_leaf 2; quest_stage q2_seven_keys 4

q2_seven_keys_runner: Veit: I run for whoever pays. Lately it's a girl with a house.
q2_seven_keys_runner_defeat: Veit: Take the slip. Read the name at the bottom before you hand it over. Just for your education.
Veit: The father confessed to protect her. She let him. That's what I call a family business.
q2_seven_keys_runner_intro: Veit: The girl sent you for the slip? She sent me for the wax. She sends well, that one.
q2_seven_keys_wait: Mina: Old Fritha in the Tackle Room fishes things out of the canal. And key cutters hide in the Smugglers' Culvert.

lines: Fishwife Marga: I pay the toll on the causeway. Then, at the far end, I pay it again. Same stamp, different hand.
Fishwife Marga: Find out who takes the second toll. I'm a widow. I can't afford to be robbed twice a day.
Fishwife Marga: The causeway has three tolls now. Progress.

q2_toll_twice_doubt: Fishwife Marga: Careful. Clever people pay a third toll in this town.
q2_toll_twice_garrick: Garrick: I'm dead. The dead pay no toll. It's the whole point.
q2_toll_twice_garrick_defeat: Garrick: Beaten. And dead. A man can only take so much in one lifetime.
Garrick: Ask Marga who sewed the wet coat. Go on. Ask.
q2_toll_twice_garrick_intro: Garrick: Marga sent you? She sends my lunch, too. Today you're the second course.

lines: Fishwife Marga: He collects on the causeway after dark. Go and collect him.
Stamp Girl Ines: One stamp is missing. Tollman Garrick's. Lost with him in the harbour two winters ago.
Stamp Girl Ines: Funny. His widow still brings his lunch to the causeway. Every evening.

q2_toll_twice_ines_after: Stamp Girl Ines: I stamp what I'm given. It's the only way to keep all ten fingers.

lines: Fishwife Marga: The lost stamp was my Garrick's? My Garrick drowned. I buried the stamp with him.
Fishwife Marga: Well. I buried a stamp. And a coffin. It was a light coffin, now that I think of it.
Fishwife Marga: You do believe I didn't know?
Fishwife Marga: You beat him? Good. Here, for a friend. The second booth is mine now. It's what he would have wanted. He isn't asked.
q2_toll_twice_reward.action: set_flag q2_toll_twice_paid; give_item strong_tonic 2; quest_stage q2_toll_twice 4

lines: Fishwife Marga: You beat him. And you think half the second toll was mine all along. Here. That's a lot of tonic for a quiet person.
q2_toll_twice_reward_doubt.action: set_flag q2_toll_twice_paid; give_item max_tonic 3; quest_stage q2_toll_twice 4

lines: Chain Boy Ruk: The second booth? It's only there at night. A man in a wet coat. He never comes from the town side.
Chain Boy Ruk: His receipts have the House stamp. The real one. Ask in the Tollhouse who's missing a stamp.

q2_toll_twice_ruk_after: Chain Boy Ruk: I pull the chain up, I let the chain down. The chain earns more than I do.
q2_toll_twice_trust: Fishwife Marga: Bless you. Nobody has believed me since the wedding.
q2_toll_twice_wait: Fishwife Marga: The chain boys on the Tollchain Causeway see who comes at night. And the stamps are kept in the Tollhouse.

lines: Skipper Hald: My boat, the Patience. Somebody sold her while I was asleep in her. I woke up a passenger.
Skipper Hald: Find out who sold my boat. A man has a right to know who robbed him. In detail.
Skipper Hald: The Patience has four owners now. She's never been so popular.

q2_two_owners_doubt: Skipper Hald: Up front? You've been in Hookwick too long already.

lines: Skipper Hald: Dame Rikke waits at the Weeping Locks with a lawyer's face. Go and argue my case.
Paint Boy Malte: The Patience? I painted 'Prudence' over her on Monday and 'Providence' on Tuesday. Same skipper paid both times.
Paint Boy Malte: The papers went down the Smugglers' Culvert, under the Weeping Locks. The rats there keep the bills of sale.

q2_two_owners_malte_after: Paint Boy Malte: I only paint names. What the names do afterwards is not my brush.

lines: Culvert Rat Smilla: Bills of sale? We keep them dry and we keep them ours. You want to read one, you get past us.

q2_two_owners_rats_after: Culvert Rat Smilla: Two sales, one mark, same hand. Hald's. He tips well. That's how we knew something was wrong.

lines: Culvert Rat Smilla: All right, all right. Here. Two bills of sale for one boat. Both signed by the skipper himself.
Skipper Hald: The bill of sale has my mark on it? Twice? Well. I do sign a lot of things.
Skipper Hald: All right. I sold her. To two buyers. A boat with two owners is the custom here, I only kept the custom.
Skipper Hald: One of them found out. Get her off my back and I'll cut you in on the third sale. You trust me?

choices.text: I want my share up front.

lines: Skipper Hald: You beat her? Partner! Here's your cut of the third sale. The buyer paid in brew. And in a boat he doesn't have yet.
q2_two_owners_reward.action: set_flag q2_two_owners_paid; give_item dash_brew 2; quest_stage q2_two_owners 4

lines: Skipper Hald: You beat her, and you counted your share before I could. Here. All of it. I feel robbed. In detail.
q2_two_owners_reward_doubt.action: set_flag q2_two_owners_paid; give_item dash_brew 4; quest_stage q2_two_owners 4

q2_two_owners_rikke: Dame Rikke: I've bought a horse. Nobody sells a horse twice. It bites.
q2_two_owners_rikke_defeat: Dame Rikke: Outbid. By a stranger. In my own lawsuit.
Dame Rikke: Keep an eye on your partner. I was his partner on Monday.
q2_two_owners_rikke_intro: Dame Rikke: Hald sent you instead of my boat. Then I'll take you instead of my money.
q2_two_owners_trust: Skipper Hald: Partner! I've never had one of those last a week.
q2_two_owners_wait: Skipper Hald: The painter's boy in the Boatshed paints over the names. And stolen hulls go through the Smugglers' Culvert under the Weeping Locks.

lines: Vigil Girl Sanne: The candles in the Vigil House have names on them. Foundry men. Three of those men walked past me this morning.
Vigil Girl Sanne: Somebody orders the candles before the accidents. Find out who. I only light them.
Wax Girl Bette: Name candles? Paid a week ahead, always. We pour them before the man is even late for supper.
Wax Girl Bette: The list comes by crow from the Rookery Cut. Ask the crow boy who writes it.

q2_wax_names_bette_after: Wax Girl Bette: We never get an order wrong. That's the frightening part.

lines: Vigil Girl Sanne: A girl's hand, round letters, a little flower on every i? Yes. That's mine.
Vigil Girl Sanne: The Syndicate says the names. I write them neatly. Neat handwriting is rare here. It pays by the name.
Vigil Girl Sanne: I asked you because the last three knew my writing. Now you do too. How do you spell your name?
You take Sanne's list and the revival leaves she kept for after work. Your name is on the list. She spelled it right.
q2_wax_names_sanne_list.action: set_flag q2_wax_names_paid; give_item revival_leaf 3; quest_stage q2_wax_names 4

q2_wax_names_sanne_list_after: Sanne: I've taken up drawing. Portraits. Very lifelike, for now.
q2_wax_names_sanne_list_defeat: Sanne: Smudged. I never smudge. You've ruined a whole page.
Sanne: Take the list. Three names are still dry. Tell them to stay home from work.
q2_wax_names_sanne_list_intro: Sanne: Hold still. I want to get the spelling right.
q2_wax_names_wait: Vigil Girl Sanne: The orders come to the Wax Hall. And the crows on the Rookery Cut carry the lists.

lines: Crow Boy Wido: The candle lists? I can't read. The crows can. They say it's a girl's hand. Round. Flowers on the i.
Crow Boy Wido: She hands them over herself, at the Vigil House door. Lights a candle after. Nice girl.

q2_wax_names_wido_after: Crow Boy Wido: The crows know everything. They just won't tell me the good parts.
rookery_cut_crowmonger: Sibbe: My crows carry letters for the Syndicate. They read them first. So do I.
rookery_cut_crowmonger_defeat: Sibbe: Return to sender. Sender's dead, but still.
rookery_cut_crowmonger_intro: Sibbe: You've got a letter on you. Let's see who it's addressed to.
rookery_cut_letter_thief: Agathe: I steal letters from the crows. Then I sell them to whoever they're about. Everyone buys.
rookery_cut_letter_thief_defeat: Agathe: Here. It says you'd win. I should read them first.
rookery_cut_letter_thief_intro: Agathe: There's a letter about you. Win and you can read it.
slag_tunnels_ash_sifter: Malve: I sift the ash for buttons. A button means a man. I have a jar of men.
slag_tunnels_ash_sifter_defeat: Malve: Keep your buttons. For now. Everyone comes through the sieve.
slag_tunnels_ash_sifter_intro: Malve: Nice buttons on that coat. Let's see how they sift.
slag_tunnels_cart_pusher: Grim: I push the cart down full and pull it up empty. Nobody asks what was in it. Good job, that.
slag_tunnels_cart_pusher_defeat: Grim: Tipped over. Like the last foreman.
slag_tunnels_cart_pusher_intro: Grim: Mind the cart. It doesn't mind you.
slag_tunnels_furnace_guard: Detlef: Brannoc pays me to guard the tunnel. The Syndicate pays me to look the other way. I squint.
slag_tunnels_furnace_guard_defeat: Detlef: I'll report I stopped you. Twice. That's two wages.
slag_tunnels_furnace_guard_intro: Detlef: Halt. One of my employers wants you stopped. I forget which.
slag_tunnels_sign: Cart tunnels under the drift. The foundry sends down what it does not want counted.
smelters_drift_slagman: Hobb: I cart slag from the foundry. Some of it used to be workers. Don't look in the cart.
smelters_drift_slagman_defeat: Hobb: Cooled off. Like everyone at the foundry, eventually.
smelters_drift_slagman_intro: Hobb: Hot day. Hot temper. Hot Spirlings.
smelters_drift_strike_breaker: Kuno: The foundry men wanted shorter days. I gave three of them very short ones.
smelters_drift_strike_breaker_defeat: Kuno: Complaint upheld. First time for everything.
smelters_drift_strike_breaker_intro: Kuno: You look like a complaint. I deal with complaints.
smugglers_culvert_bilge_boy: Arne: I bail the culvert. It fills again. It's the steadiest job in Vellmarch.
smugglers_culvert_bilge_boy_defeat: Arne: Soaked again. At least that's honest work.
smugglers_culvert_bilge_boy_intro: Arne: You're dry. Nobody down here is dry. Suspicious.
smugglers_culvert_crate_runner: Isolde: These crates are empty. Write that down. The heavy ones are extra empty.
smugglers_culvert_crate_runner_defeat: Isolde: Fine. You saw nothing. I'll even pay you to have seen it.
smugglers_culvert_crate_runner_intro: Isolde: You saw the crates. Now you carry one or you carry bruises.
smugglers_culvert_sign: A brick drain under the locks. Everything the canal loses turns up here, with a price tag.
smugglers_culvert_tide_clerk: Bodo: I keep the Syndicate's books down here. Damp books. The numbers run.
smugglers_culvert_tide_clerk_defeat: Bodo: Balanced. I'll enter you under 'losses'.
smugglers_culvert_tide_clerk_intro: Bodo: An audit? Down here we settle audits by hand.
tallowmarket_folk_1: Wick Boy Tam: I sell candles to the vigil for the foundry workers. Same customers every year. Fewer each time.
tallowmarket_folk_2: Weigher Odo: Rumours are sold by weight. Yours is light. Nobody's lied about you yet.
tallowmarket_folk_3: Syndicate Runner Pell: I don't work for the Syndicate. Write that down. Then burn it.

lines: Chandler Mags: Rest by the wax vats. Warm, quiet, and only slightly flammable.

tallowmarket_rumour_room_broker: Whisperer Nell: I heard you were coming. I sold that before you arrived.
tallowmarket_sign: Tallowmarket. Candles by day. Do not ask what is sold by night.

lines: Rumour Broker Fenn: Tonics on the left, gossip on the right. The gossip costs more and works better.
tallowmarket_trader.action: shop strong_tonic max_tonic remedy cooling_gel wake_bell revival_leaf dash_brew guard_brew pith_mend pith_clear

tallowmarket_vigil_house_widow: Vigil Keeper Dorn: One candle for each foundry worker. We ran out of shelves last winter.
tallowmarket_wax_hall_chandler: Chandler Ruth: Every candle here burns for someone. Pick a short one. They're cheaper.
tallowmarket_weigh_house_weigher: Weigher Ansel: The scales are honest. The weights are a family heirloom. Different family.
tithe_road_alms_seller: Trude: I sell alms. You pay me, I feel sorry for you. It's cheaper than the House.
tithe_road_alms_seller_defeat: Trude: Poor me. Finally the pity goes the right way.
tithe_road_alms_seller_intro: Trude: No coin? Then I'll take pity out of your team.
tithe_road_tithecollector: Prue: The House takes a tenth. The Syndicate takes a tenth. I take what's left, for safekeeping.
tithe_road_tithecollector_defeat: Prue: Paid in full. I'll forge you a receipt.
tithe_road_tithecollector_intro: Prue: Your tithe is overdue. I accept payment in battle.
tollchain_causeway_chain_inspector: Lorenz: I inspect the toll chain. Every link is a family that couldn't pay. It's a long chain.
tollchain_causeway_chain_inspector_defea: Lorenz: In order. I'll stamp your forehead. No? Suit yourself.
tollchain_causeway_chain_inspector_intro: Lorenz: Your papers. No papers? Then your Spirlings will do.
tollchain_causeway_tollkeeper: Vos: The causeway is free. Crossing it isn't.
tollchain_causeway_tollkeeper_defeat: Vos: Fine. Pass. I'll bill the House for my pride.
tollchain_causeway_tollkeeper_intro: Vos: Pay the toll in coin or in bruises. I take both.
vault_rift_acolyte: Barra: Corin counts every coin twice. The second time he counts you.
vault_rift_acolyte_defeat: Barra: Fine. He's expecting you. He paid for the barge, remember.
vault_rift_acolyte_intro: Barra: Your purse or your pride. Corin takes both, I just take the first.
vault_rift_sign: The vault under Lastlamp. The walls are lined with coins that hum like bees.

lines: Cold water seeps between the stones. It tastes of iron and old debts.
Your Spirlings drink and rest.
Rust eats the foundry from the inside. Brannoc says the Syndicate did it. The Syndicate says Brannoc did.
Your fixer Wren tipped off the Syndicate. Her cut was your route, your team and your bedtime.

warden_brannoc_defeat: You beat the foundry. Now guess who told the Syndicate you were coming.
warden_brannoc_intro: My furnace, my rules. The rules say you burn.

lines: The vault under Lastlamp hums with stolen colour. The man who paid for your barge waits inside.
Corin never wanted the Rifts closed. He wanted them owned. Trust no one, least of all your sponsor.

warden_corin_defeat: Keep the vault. I keep the town. Nobody wins clean in Vellmarch.
warden_corin_intro: I funded the barge, the bribes and your little tour. Every coin comes home, kid.

lines: The canal locks bleed water into the street. Odile keeps the Lock Rift and the only key.
Odile copied the key and sold it to the Tallow Syndicate before she even fought you.

warden_odile_defeat: Fine. Take the key. Just know I already sold a copy.
warden_odile_intro: You came all this way for a lock keeper? Sweet. The House pays me to lose slowly.

lines: At the masked opera every guest is someone else. Sable offers a truce, a drink and a lie, in that order.
The Syndicate sells Wren out in turn. She ends up at your door with nothing but a sorry and a spare key.

warden_sable_defeat: Bravo. Now take off yours. Oh. You were never wearing one. How dull.
warden_sable_intro: Everyone in this opera wears a face. Mine is the only honest one, and it is fake.
weeping_locks_lock_gambler: Ewald: I bet on which lock floods next. I lost the house. Then I bet on the house.
weeping_locks_lock_gambler_defeat: Ewald: Nothing it is. I'm used to it.
weeping_locks_lock_gambler_intro: Ewald: Double or nothing. You're the nothing.
weeping_locks_sluicer: Morwen: The locks weep because Odile pays them to. The rest of us weep for free.
weeping_locks_sluicer_defeat: Morwen: Soaked and beaten. By you. That's new.
weeping_locks_sluicer_intro: Morwen: Nobody passes the locks dry. Let's get you wet.

lines: Fixer Wren Marlow meets you off the barge with a grin and a map. The House of Corin wants the Rifts closed, and they pay well.
Wren: First job: the Lock Rift past Hookwick, west gate. Odile has the key. Ask nicely, then don't.

wren_after: The free barge was a delivery: you. The bargeman gets paid twice, once by each House.
